summary.oneLiner: The deck positions M&M as a multi-engine group — market-leading Auto (SUV/LCV) and Farm franchises plus Finance, Tech and "Growth Gems" (Real Estate, Accelo, Logistics, Trucks & Buses, Aerostructures) — delivering "Acceleration in Uncertainty" through commodity inflation via scale, leadership share and an AI-led transformation.
summary.business: M&M manufactures motor vehicles, trailers, semi-trailers and other transport vehicles alongside tractors and farm equipment, with Automotive contributing 75.01% and Farm Equipment 24.99% of turnover under the BRSR products/services disclosure. The Automotive business spans utility vehicles and SUVs (ICE and electric), light and heavy commercial vehicles, three-wheelers and last-mile mobility, while the Farm business sells tractors under the Mahindra, Swaraj and Trakstar brands. The Company serves urban and rural customers, government agencies, corporates, SMEs, agricultural and non-agricultural businesses and tours and travel operators across 28 States and 6 Union Territories, with exports contributing 4.11% of total turnover.

Platforms and architectures: Vision.S, Vision.T, Vision.SXT and Vision.X SUV concepts

currentContext.expansion: M&M's stated capacity plan supports a product roadmap running to 2031 that comprises 10 LCV launches (including new products based on the Veero platform and portfolio upgrades) and 16 SUVs (10 ICE and 6 electric). In the near term the strategy, anchored on the theme 'Accelerate in Uncertainty', is to fortify the core through capacity debottlenecking in FY27 alongside supply chain de-risking and a commodity hedging programme. Beyond that, phased NU_IQ capacity is coming up at Chakan by FY28, and a new greenfield plant in Nagpur with 5 lakh vehicle capacity is planned for CY28 and beyond; the Chairman notes the Mahindra Group has announced one of the largest prospective investments in its history in Nagpur, at Rs. 15,000 crore over 10 years. This is complemented by a push on sales and service infrastructure, with 450+ touchpoints added over the past two years and a continued scale-up planned, and by simultaneous strengthening of charging infrastructure under Mahindra Charge_iN, whose open-source platform carries a commitment to deploy 1,000 fast-charging points along major corridors by 2027. EV capacity expansion and multi-year capital commitments to product development and international expansion are also cited, as are ongoing investments in products that meet future emission regulations ahead of the TREM Stage V transition.

risks.risk: Monsoon and weather dependence of farm demand
risks.note: India is expected to receive a below-normal southwest monsoon in 2026 on potential El Nino conditions, with IMD projecting rainfall at around 92% of the Long Period Average; positive Indian Ocean Dipole conditions could partially offset this. Management argues the farm ecosystem is now more resilient - horticulture penetration, non-farm income, government support, mechanisation, higher MSPs and farm credit - and that the historical correlation between monsoon variability and Company performance has been relatively moderate.

Commodity prices fluctuated significantly in FY26 due to global supply-demand imbalances, policy uncertainties and geopolitical disruptions. Mitigated through value engineering, supplier negotiations and long-term price contracts, plus hedging under Board-approved foreign exchange and commodity risk management policies.

risks.risk: Geopolitical disruption and crude oil / shipping-route exposure
risks.note: The West Asia conflict poses a near-term risk to the Indian auto sector through crude oil price volatility, disruption of critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and supply constraints in oil-linked raw materials; prolonged uncertainty could heighten inflationary pressure and currency volatility. De-risking relies on localisation, buffers for critical components, supplier diversification, optimised use of high-risk materials and long-term supply contracts.

risks.risk: Emission and safety regulation transition (TREM Stage V)
risks.note: Agricultural tractors above 75 HP and below 25 HP move to TREM Stage V from 1st October 2026; the 25-50 HP segment migrates to TREM IIIAA from April 2028 and the entire 25-75 HP band moves to TREM V from April 2032. Compliance requires ongoing investment in compliant product development; industry leaders also emphasise the need for stable EV-related policy frameworks to support long-range vehicle programmes.

International tractor markets saw subdued growth in FY26, with cost-side pressure on farmer profitability dampening farm machinery capex and softening replacement demand particularly in North America and parts of Europe. In Latin America, near-term Brazilian demand was hit by volatile commodity prices, higher financing costs and weather uncertainty, while currency volatility in select emerging markets pressured affordability and delayed farmer investment decisions.

India applies a tax-rate differential between small and large passenger vehicles based on vehicle length, engine size and fuel type, and the Company's flagship products attract higher tax rates. Mitigated by strengthening the lower-tax UV portfolio (XUV3X0, Bolero Neo, Bolero, Thar) and by EVs (XEV 9S, XEV 9e, BE 6, XUV 3XO EV, XUV 400) which attract the least GST among passenger vehicle categories.

risks.risk: Resource circularity and Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) compliance
risks.note: Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk: evolving EPR mandates for end-of-life vehicles, plastics, batteries and e-waste create compliance risk and operational challenges compounded by general waste management obligations, and involve increased compliance costs and investment in waste infrastructure and traceability. Addressed through CERO Recycling vehicle takebacks, onboarding lithium-ion battery recyclers and authorised plastic recyclers, used-oil collection via dealerships and supplier engagement.

Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk: operating in water-stressed geographies exposes the Company to resource scarcity, operational disruption and regulatory restrictions, and water management is described as critical to long-term production stability. Mitigated through rainwater harvesting, Zero Liquid Discharge installations and water recycling initiatives across sites.

one-line thesis: The federation, not the SUV, is now the earnings engine: consolidated PAT +34% with every engine firing — Auto PAT +21%, Farm PAT +15%, Mahindra Finance +78%, Tech Mahindra +28% and Growth Gems profit 3x — delivered through a 400–500bps commodity shock. Auto core margin fell to 8.9% PBIT (from 10.2%/10.8%), and management explicitly called Q1 the low point with 1.5% + 2.7% price hikes already taken and an 85bps hedging MTM loss that reverses as a buffer. The real forward story is capacity: 64.5k → 68k vehicles/month by Sep-26, 82k by end-FY27, and a 2x by FY31 ladder through Chakan and Nagpur, because the constraint today is supply, not demand.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > Adjustments / one-offs to strip out: (a) CIE gain on sale flows through investments — ex-CIE consolidated PAT growth is +22%, not 34%; use 22%. (b) Farm consolidated PBIT carries an impairment on Erkunt Foundry and one more international company — +9% reported vs +12% pre-impairment; the foundry problem is "solved for and exited," so this should not recur. (c) Auto carried an 85bps QoQ hedging MTM loss on aluminium/precious metals — reported 7.1% margin implies ~8% underlying, and management conceded that framing was "a fair point." Critically this loss exists because commodities crashed in the last 10 days of the quarter, so it is a buffer, not a wound. (d) Farm Q2 faces a festive-season shift (Navratri from Q2 last year to 11-Oct this year) — a pure operating-leverage timing effect, not demand loss.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: Auto margin: "sequentially if there is no further dramatic change in commodities from where we are, we think we should be able to maintain/slightly improve the Operating Profit margin between Q1 and Q2." Framed repeatedly as "Q1 in Auto was a low point and it should improve from here." Management pushed back on the analyst's 600–700bps headwind math: "I wouldn't get to 600-700. I think 400-500 is what we saw in Q1."

Farm margin: deliberately NOT guided up — "some temporary blip is likely in Farm" in Q2 on unhedgeable steel (+24%) and rubber (+30%, +53% since the start of the calendar year) plus the festive shift. Recovery pinned to Q3: "as we get into Q3 we are hoping that there will be some softening on commodities plus we also get into season upcycle."

Pricing already taken: Auto ~1.5% earlier + 2.7% average in mid-July (deliberately one large hike rather than repeated small ones). Farm ~₹15,000 in August. Headroom exists because post-GST-cut prices "still continue to be below what they were in September, October last year."
ROE: target held at 18% despite printing 23% — "we are not resetting expectations."

Capacity (dated ladder): 60k ICE + 8k EV = 68k/month operationally ready by September 2026 (end of H1). By end-FY27: 70k ICE + 12k EV = 82k/month, the +10k ICE and +4k EV specifically for NUIQ platform launch and a new EV in FY28. Then +10k at Chakan → 92k for NUIQ phase 2, then Nagpur +20k/month, first phase ready H1 CY2029, second phase 10–12 months later. Net: 2x capacity between now and FY31.

EV economics: already EBITDA positive without PLI. Cost curve from localisation + supplier scale to "kick in in the next 12 to 18 months." Pricing power arrives after 20–25% industry EV penetration, at which point "a reasonable premium of 5–7% is possible" vs today's near-parity.

PLI: management expects the subsidy to taper — "as we start showing higher margins with scale, PLI should reduce… we would not want to make super normal profits based on subsidies." Clarity on timelines in 6–12 months. No absolute PLI amount disclosed.
Tech Mahindra: 15% EBIT margin by end-FY27, then a new phase announced.

Mahindra Finance: ₹3 lakh crore book by 2031 with a 70:30 mobility:non-wheels mix; ROA band 2.2–2.5% (at 2.4% now); ROE first milestone 15%. Used-vehicle disbursement share to climb back to 16–19% of incremental disbursements.
Mahindra Lifespaces: ₹10,000 cr pre-sales by FY30 (14x FY20); top-3/top-5 relative market share in Mumbai, Pune, Bangalore only.
Mahindra Logistics: remaining 2 lakh sq ft of white space to be sold by September; RIVIGO express EBITDA-positive "just around the corner" — CEO explicitly declined to name a month.
Aerostructures: Global Investor Day aspiration of 30x growth in a decade (10x organic) — "I can assure you we will grow faster than that."
order book & pipeline: Not an order-book business at the parent, but three hard pipeline metrics were given:

Aerostructures — $1.2 bn cumulative contract wins, of which $600 mn in the last year alone. Two large Airbus deals recently; single-source globally for the fuselage of two helicopters. Vinod Sahay's framing is the useful one: the industry takes 2–3 years to industrialise an award, so the book runs far ahead of revenue — "from an order-book standpoint we are actually a much bigger player than our revenue right now," against a global #1 sitting at ~4–4.5 (bn).

Real Estate GDV — ₹50,000 cr pipeline, up from ₹8,000 cr three years ago; ₹5,600 cr added this quarter alone (+60%), pre-sales ₹925 cr (2x). Anish Shah's point is that this fuel is already acquired — "the future growth is going to be driven by what we already have in place." Includes multi-use projects of ₹5,000 cr up to ₹10,000–12,000 cr each.

Auto demand vs supply — management refused to disclose enquiry/booking growth by powertrain or GST bracket ("it kind of gives an indication of… where demand momentum is"), conceding only "very strong demand momentum, urban and rural both." Dealer physical inventory ~15 days — thin, confirming the constraint is production not offtake. Tractor channel inventory 30–40 days, in line with norms (Swaraj below norm on supply issues).
segment / subsidiary detail: Auto — the new 3-column disclosure. For the first time management split auto into (1) core = ICE SUV + LCV, domestic + exports, at 8.9% PBIT; (2) EV = Mahindra Electric + M&M conversion income, at 5.3% / ₹288 cr PBIT; (3) others = trucks & buses, contract manufacturing for Last Mile Mobility, domestic + international subs. This is a material transparency upgrade — the ICE core margin was previously buried inside a blended number.
SUV — volumes +14.9% on an exceptional 22.1% Q1 FY26 base, despite production losses in April and May. Revenue market share held at the 24–25% line (LY Q1 was an outlier high).
LCV — volumes +20%, market share growing sequentially; #2 in <12t LCV bus (up from #3).

Trucks & Buses — volume +11%, market share 7.8%, but flagged as seasonally flattered: "market share is much higher for us in quarter one… because SML has a very strong bus queue, and the bus market is rallying in quarter one."
Last Mile Mobility (L5/3W) — volume 42,000, #1 position held, and the standout stat: L5 EV penetration at 40% vs ~27% a year ago, driven by the UDO.

EV / Born-Electric. Penetration 12% vs industry 9%; volumes +77%; XEV 9S is the single largest-selling EV across all passenger vehicles by volume despite its premium price point — management repeated this twice, and it is the strongest evidence they have that BEV demand is no longer price-floor-driven. Cumulative 77,000 EVs sold. The INGLO platform is the profitability lever: developed for a small number of vehicles but usable "across multiple top hats," so incremental model capex is low. Anish Shah's scale argument: ICE is running 9x EV volumes, and even at 1x the EV business is profitable ex-PLI.

Farm Equipment. Volume +18%, exports +15%, core tractor margin 19.2% inside the 17–19% band management says has held through both up- and down-cycles ("we have rarely gone below 17%, except maybe one quarter"). Farm machinery had its highest-ever quarter at ₹370 cr revenue — the mechanisation thesis showing up in the P&L. Horsepower mix has shifted hard: ~69–70% now in the 40–50 HP band, pulled by seeders and balers and helped by post-GST affordability ("they are able to buy a product with a higher horsepower for a price that they would have paid for a lower horsepower earlier"). International subsidiaries are the sore spot — a loss including the Erkunt Foundry impairment, now "solved for and exited," with remaining "weak spots" internationally acknowledged as a fix-list.

Rural demand construct (management's own six-point enabler chart): accelerating farm-labour shortage pushing mechanisation; wheat procurement +19% strengthening Rabi cash flows; rainfall deficit narrowed to 15% from much worse in June; reservoirs 7% below LPA but recovering; Kharif sowing shortfall only ~4%; government spending +16% plus state spends. Conclusion: "the data indicates a lot of negativity if you just look at the rainfall deficit, but because rains have actually come in, the sentiment is not negative."
Services & Growth Gems.

Mahindra Finance — PAT +78%; NIM rebuilt 6.5% → 7.3%; ROA 2.4%; GS2+GS3 below 10% for 7 consecutive quarters, GS2 (30+) down 100bps YoY. Book ~₹1.5 lakh cr, 83% wheels / 17% non-wheels; non-wheels +79%, housing finance +130% with housing GS3 now below 2.5%. Wheels growing ~20%. Used vehicles = 16% of incremental disbursements last quarter (band 15–19%), deliberately throttled while residual values reset post-GST; #1 in used tractor, #2–3 in used car.
Tech Mahindra — PAT +28%, EBIT margin 14.4%, FCF +94%, large-deal-led; geographic diversification and margin-gap closure the stated levers.

Mahindra Lifespaces — GDV +₹5,600 cr this quarter, pipeline ₹50,000 cr, pre-sales ₹925 cr (2x), OCs delivered ahead of schedule — 3,000 apartments OC'd, 1,500 delivered, 99% "zero-snag". Strategy is deliberately narrow: three cities (Mumbai/Pune/Bangalore = 55% of national unit volume), mid-premium and premium only, affordable exited. Measured on relative market share vs the biggest player, not absolute share. Slum redevelopment explicitly not prioritised today.

Mahindra Logistics — ₹14 cr profit at the M&M level, ₹25 cr at the business level — highest ever quarterly profit, after 11 straight quarters of losses through Q2 last year. The single biggest lever was white space cut from 16 lakh sq ft to 2 lakh sq ft, all sold not surrendered. RIVIGO express losses cut sharply, still a drag. Three very large e-com sites started this month. LOGIFREIGHT platform launched with ~5 customers signalling implementation.

Mahindra Aerostructures — see §4. Moving up the value chain from detailed parts → sub-assemblies → full fuselages, i.e. "from a manufacturer who used to make thousands of small parts, to making hundreds of high-value parts." Rated top-5 globally on quality/business excellence. An overseas acquisition is explicitly on the table, to be underwritten on returns.

SML Mahindra (truck & bus combination, announced 29-Jul-2026) — described as accretive, doubling the business's size, with network, product, cost and value-engineering synergies "already started working."
Mahindra Accelo — named as one of the three Growth Gems driving the +39% revenue / 3x profit, but not detailed on this call.
Not discussed on this call: Mahindra Holidays (MHRIL), Classic Legends, Mahindra Susten.
growth verticals / optionality: NUIQ platform — a new architecture opening "a segment we really haven't played in in a big way." First product launches in FY28; the entire +10k ICE capacity added by end-FY27 and a further +10k at Chakan are earmarked for it. This is the largest undisclosed swing factor in the FY28 story — management has not named the segment.
Nagpur greenfield — +20k/month in phase 1 (H1 CY2029) plus a second phase 10–12 months later; the back half of the 2x-by-FY31 plan.

AI as an operating layer, with disclosed outcomes — Paint.ai (paint consumption, rework, effective capacity); Service.ai across 2,600 workshop assistants; Reach.ai delivering 91,000 AI-originated test drives that management calls "direct addition to revenue"; simulation for drag coefficient cut from 10 hours to 2 minutes; welding validation across 300 guns / 20,000 welds per hour at Chakan replacing destructive monthly sampling. In Finance: SamurAI processes 65% of loan files and cuts TAT ~40%; 5 lakh+ service requests fulfilled; 30% lower cross-sell acquisition cost; Voice.ai in collections and sales. Farm is piloting sentiment.ai to harvest village-level field-force sentiment. Foundation: 50 forward-deployed engineers, 19 proprietary models, 1,900 leaders trained, 15 large transformation projects, plus group and business AI governance councils.
Non-wheels lending adjacency — Mahindra Finance's mortgage/SME/PL push, framed as "diversification within adjacency" for the Bharat customer rather than a new market.
Industrial real estate — Lifespaces expanding the IC portfolio as a counter-cyclical complement to residential.
6a. moat & competitive position: Brand trust priced in cash. "Our Lifespaces business can price 15% higher in the market with very strong competitors because of trust," and a joint-development partner closed a ₹12,000 cr GDV opportunity saying "I am just going to work with Mahindra, I don't care what other people give me." That is a rare, quantified brand-premium disclosure — and it is being harvested by a non-auto business off the auto brand.

Proprietary AI built on owned data and owned GPUs. Asked directly by Kapil where differentiation comes from when "these same AI models are available to everyone," the answer was data and process ownership: "you feed in 20 years of your simulation data into it. Then it becomes a different AI. That AI is known only to you." Applications run on owned GPUs — "we don't need to pay for tokens for this" — so the unit economics of scaling AI don't degrade with usage. Mahindra Finance's version is the 3.8 lakh villages / multi-dialect unstructured data corpus "which was never harnessed before."

Tractor margin band as evidence of pricing discipline. 17–19% held "irrespective of what is happening to these 2 key variables" (industry cycle, commodity cycle) — and 19.2% delivered inside a 300bps+ commodity shock.

Aerostructures reputational barrier. Parts must last the ~40-year life of an airframe, industrialisation takes 2–3 years, and the qualification is reputational: "this is an industry where your reputation counts over everything else." Anish Shah's own words: "a very strong moat around it that no one can really come into."

EV word-of-mouth flywheel. The XEV 9S outselling every other PV EV despite its price point is the demonstration that Mahindra has crossed from subsidy-led to product-led EV demand ahead of the industry (12% vs 9%).
margins & cost dynamics: The quarter's whole margin story is one number absorbed: 450bps of commodity inflation in Auto and 300+bps in Farm, against which Auto gave up only 160–170bps of margin. The CFO called that "remarkable" and attributed it to proactive pricing (1.5% + 2.7%) plus operating-cost actions.

1. Auto is hedged, Farm is not. Aluminium and precious metals are hedged; steel and rubber cannot be hedged, and those are precisely Farm's inputs — steel +24%, rubber +30% (+53% since the start of the calendar year). This is why Auto is guided to improve and Farm is guided to blip.

2. The hedging loss is a good loss. The 85bps QoQ MTM hit came from commodities crashing in the final ~10 days of the quarter after the war-halt announcement — "you had a disproportionate loss in 10 days." Anish Shah: "we like the loss in this case because it meant the commodity prices came down sharply," and it "gives us a buffer as well for the next quarter." Rajesh Jejurikar's counter-caution was sharper: "don't bake anything in because there's so much volatility."

3. The GST cushion is finite. The 2.7% hike was affordable only because "prices still continue to be below what they were in September, October last year" thanks to the GST reduction. That headroom is now partly consumed.

EV margin (5.3%) sits below ICE (8.9%) but is rising with scale and is positive before PLI. Farm's operating-leverage risk in Q2 is not price but calendar: the festive shift to 11-Oct moves peak tractor volume from Q2 to Q3.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): The capacity ladder is the most checkable thing on this call:

Slippage risk is explicitly supplier-side and was volunteered, not extracted: "there is a new black swan literally every other day." Named disruptions this quarter — 3 days of production lost in July to Maharashtra flooding (at least 2 days across all plants), a plant shutdown already scheduled in July, and a fire at a very large supplier in the South cutting off a critical part. "It didn't allow us to build inventory as well." The 8k EV capacity is also mix-exposed: "there's one product out of the three which is doing disproportionately well," so nameplate readiness ≠ shippable mix.
capital allocation: ROE is the discipline. 18% group target, 23% delivered, target deliberately not raised. Businesses are held to "profit standards… we need to be able to maintain ROA," with explicit long-duration leeway granted where the asset justifies it — aerospace was given a 10–15 year runway to profitability.

Exits are real, not rhetorical. Erkunt Foundry impaired and exited; Mahindra CIE stake sold (the gain sits in investments this quarter); Lifespaces exited the affordable segment. Anish Shah recounted the truck & bus history as the template: "Let's decide whether we want this business or not… if they cannot, we will exit" — the business executed, so it got SML instead of the axe.
Inorganic is live in exactly one place: a global acquisition in Aerostructures, to be underwritten on returns, driven by what OEM customers want Mahindra to become.
SML Mahindra combination described as accretive with cost/value-engineering synergies.
No dividend, buyback, leverage or consolidated-capex-rupee number was given on this call.
risks & watch-items: Commodity volatility, unhedgeable in Farm. Steel +24%, rubber +30% (+53% CYTD). Management's own hedge against being wrong: "if you believe the war is going to continue for the next 6 months, then we may have bigger problems, the whole economy… will have bigger problems."

Supply-chain fragility is the binding constraint on the capacity ladder. Stated capacity includes supplier capacity, "and that's not always happening." Fire at a South supplier, floods, and shutdowns all hit inside one month.
Farm Q2 is pre-warned down on the festive shift + commodities — the one place management refused to guide optimistically.

PLI taper is management's own base case. They are voluntarily telling the government the subsidy should shrink as EV margins scale. EV margin at 5.3% is not yet ICE-level, so the taper timing (clarity in 6–12 months) is a genuine earnings variable.
Monsoon still unresolved. 15% rainfall deficit, reservoirs 7% below LPA, Kharif sowing ~4% behind. "We need to see what happens to rainfall and other factors over the next two months."
Farm market share slipped off the 45.2% all-time high — acknowledged, not explained.
International farm subsidiaries remain loss-making beyond Erkunt; "we still have a certain set of weak spots."
RIVIGO express is still a drag with no dated turnaround — CEO deliberately withheld a month.
EV mix concentration — one of three EV products is doing "disproportionately well," so capacity readiness may not convert.
Disclosure withheld: absolute PLI contribution, enquiry/booking growth by powertrain or GST bracket, and consolidated absolute revenue/PAT on the call.
management quality / tone: The tell of this call is the format change: Anish Shah put seven business CEOs on stage — Sahay, Sikka, Nakra, Sinha, Velusamy, Rebello — and said it will be the format going forward, so investors "yourself be able to assess the quality of talent that we have." A holdco discount is fundamentally a bet against management depth; putting the bench on stage is a direct, structural answer to it.

Tone was "cautiously optimistic" — the exact phrase used to open and close. Specific credibility markers: refusing to reset the 18% ROE target upward after a 23% print; volunteering the ex-CIE 22% number rather than letting 34% stand; disclosing the auto 3-column margin split for the first time, which exposes the 8.9% core rather than hiding it; conceding the hedging-adjusted ~8% underlying margin when an analyst constructed it; and pushing back numerically rather than vaguely when Binay built a 650–700bps headwind ("I wouldn't get to 600-700. I think 400-500"). Jejurikar volunteered the July production losses with visible reluctance ("I was avoiding wanting to say this") — unforced disclosure of bad news.

Where they closed up: Jejurikar bluntly refused the enquiry/booking cut — "You really want to know everything about our business… it kind of gives an indication of… where demand momentum is." Sikka refused to date the RIVIGO breakeven. Shah refused a PLI timeline. Each refusal was stated as a refusal, not disguised as an answer.
non-obvious takeaways: The 34% PAT headline is 22% after the CIE gain — and management said so unprompted. Anyone anchoring on 34% is anchoring on an asset sale. The genuinely impressive number is that 22% was delivered while eating 450bps of auto commodity inflation.

The hedging loss is bullish, and the market will likely read it backwards. An 85bps MTM loss on aluminium hedges exists only because spot aluminium fell ~20% in 8–10 days. The loss is the receipt for the input relief that shows up in Q2 COGS. Reported margin 7.1%, underlying ~8%, and the delta reverses.

First-time 3-column disclosure is a governance signal disguised as a slide. Splitting core ICE (8.9%) from EV (5.3%) from others removes management's own ability to hide EV dilution inside a blended number. Companies volunteer that structure when they expect the split to improve — i.e. it's a forward-confidence tell about EV margin convergence.

The Lifespaces "15% price premium on trust" is the group's most under-priced asset. A real-estate developer monetising an automotive brand's trust is textbook conglomerate synergy that almost never actually shows up in numbers. The ₹12,000 cr JDA won on brand alone is the same asset in a second form.

Owned GPUs change the AI unit economics. "We don't need to pay for tokens" means AI deployment scales at fixed cost, not variable cost — the opposite of peers renting frontier-model inference. Combined with 19 proprietary models trained on 20 years of proprietary simulation data, this is a cost and differentiation position, and it is invisible in the P&L today.

L5 EV penetration at 40% (from 27%) is running ~3x the PV rate and gets a single line on the call. Last Mile Mobility is quietly the group's most electrified business and its economics are TCO-driven — a far more durable adoption base than PV.

Mahindra Finance's Q1 PAT contribution exceeded Farm's (213 vs Farm's, per the contribution chart Shah pointed at). The market still prices M&M as an SUV-and-tractor company; the earnings mix has already moved.
Season shift to 11-Oct means Q2 tractor volume is arithmetically pre-committed to disappoint and Q3 to flatter. Any read on FY27 farm demand off the Q2 print alone will be wrong in both directions.

The capacity plan is a demand statement in disguise. Committing to 2x by FY31 with Nagpur greenfield only makes sense if management believes today's 15-day dealer inventory is structural, not cyclical.

This call confirms and quantifies all four of those profile themes for the first time: EV penetration 12% vs industry 9% with EV PBIT ₹288 cr; rural enabler chart (wheat procurement +19%, govt spend +16%, deficit narrowed to 15%); AI with disclosed outcome metrics on owned GPUs; SUV volume +14.9% with revenue market share at 24–25%. It also materially extends the profile: the sub-segment list must now carry Growth Gems (Real Estate, Logistics, Aerostructures, Accelo) and Last Mile Mobility, and the entity list must add SML Mahindra (combination announced 29-Jul-2026) while dropping Mahindra CIE (stake sold) and Erkunt Foundry (impaired and exited). Headline: consolidated PAT +34% (+22% ex-CIE gain), revenue +28%, ROE 23% vs 18% target, EPS ₹48. Auto core PBIT margin compressed to 8.9% (from 10.2%/10.8%) on 450bps commodity inflation plus an 85bps hedging MTM loss; Farm consolidated 14.2% with core tractor at 19.2%. Every subsidiary engine positive: MMFS +78%, TechM +28%, Growth Gems 3x. Capacity ladder set out for the first time in dated form: 64.5k → 68k by Sep-26 → 82k by end-FY27 → 92k → 2x by FY31 with Nagpur phase 1 in H1 CY2029.

Q2 FY27 → check: (1) did Auto OPM "maintain/slightly improve" sequentially off the 7.1% reported / ~8% hedge-adjusted base, as promised — and did the 85bps hedging loss actually reverse into a buffer; (2) did Farm deliver only the pre-warned "temporary blip," or worse, given the 11-Oct festive shift moved peak tractor volume into Q3; (3) was 68,000 units/month capacity operationally ready by September (60k ICE + 8k EV) — this is the first hard, dated commitment to test; (4) did the 2.7% July auto price hike stick without demand damage (dealer inventory was only ~15 days); (5) Mahindra Logistics — were the last 2 lakh sq ft of white space sold by September, and did RIVIGO express turn EBITDA positive ("just around the corner"); (6) Farm market share vs the 45.2% all-time high, and whether international subs stopped bleeding post-Erkunt exit; (7) any PLI-taper clarity inside the stated 6–12 month window; (8) monsoon resolution against the 15% deficit / 4% Kharif sowing shortfall; (9) did EV penetration hold above 12% and did the XEV 9S keep the #1 PV-EV slot; (10) NUIQ segment finally named ahead of the FY28 launch.

one-line thesis: The federation, not the SUV, is now the earnings engine: consolidated PAT +34% with every engine firing — Auto PAT +21%, Farm PAT +15%, Mahindra Finance +78%, Tech Mahindra +28% and Growth Gems profit 3x — delivered through a 400–500bps commodity shock. Auto core margin fell to 8.9% PBIT (from 10.2%/10.8%), and management explicitly called Q1 the low point with 1.5% + 2.7% price hikes already taken and an 85bps hedging MTM loss that reverses as a buffer. The real forward story is capacity: 64.5k → 68k vehicles/month by Sep-26, 82k by end-FY27, and a 2x by FY31 ladder through Chakan and Nagpur, because the constraint today is supply, not demand.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > Adjustments / one-offs to strip out: (a) CIE gain on sale flows through investments — ex-CIE consolidated PAT growth is +22%, not 34%; use 22%. (b) Farm consolidated PBIT carries an impairment on Erkunt Foundry and one more international company — +9% reported vs +12% pre-impairment; the foundry problem is "solved for and exited," so this should not recur. (c) Auto carried an 85bps QoQ hedging MTM loss on aluminium/precious metals — reported 7.1% margin implies ~8% underlying, and management conceded that framing was "a fair point." Critically this loss exists because commodities crashed in the last 10 days of the quarter, so it is a buffer, not a wound. (d) Farm Q2 faces a festive-season shift (Navratri from Q2 last year to 11-Oct this year) — a pure operating-leverage timing effect, not demand loss.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: Auto margin: "sequentially if there is no further dramatic change in commodities from where we are, we think we should be able to maintain/slightly improve the Operating Profit margin between Q1 and Q2." Framed repeatedly as "Q1 in Auto was a low point and it should improve from here." Management pushed back on the analyst's 600–700bps headwind math: "I wouldn't get to 600-700. I think 400-500 is what we saw in Q1."

Farm margin: deliberately NOT guided up — "some temporary blip is likely in Farm" in Q2 on unhedgeable steel (+24%) and rubber (+30%, +53% since the start of the calendar year) plus the festive shift. Recovery pinned to Q3: "as we get into Q3 we are hoping that there will be some softening on commodities plus we also get into season upcycle."

Pricing already taken: Auto ~1.5% earlier + 2.7% average in mid-July (deliberately one large hike rather than repeated small ones). Farm ~₹15,000 in August. Headroom exists because post-GST-cut prices "still continue to be below what they were in September, October last year."
ROE: target held at 18% despite printing 23% — "we are not resetting expectations."

Capacity (dated ladder): 60k ICE + 8k EV = 68k/month operationally ready by September 2026 (end of H1). By end-FY27: 70k ICE + 12k EV = 82k/month, the +10k ICE and +4k EV specifically for NUIQ platform launch and a new EV in FY28. Then +10k at Chakan → 92k for NUIQ phase 2, then Nagpur +20k/month, first phase ready H1 CY2029, second phase 10–12 months later. Net: 2x capacity between now and FY31.

EV economics: already EBITDA positive without PLI. Cost curve from localisation + supplier scale to "kick in in the next 12 to 18 months." Pricing power arrives after 20–25% industry EV penetration, at which point "a reasonable premium of 5–7% is possible" vs today's near-parity.

PLI: management expects the subsidy to taper — "as we start showing higher margins with scale, PLI should reduce… we would not want to make super normal profits based on subsidies." Clarity on timelines in 6–12 months. No absolute PLI amount disclosed.
Tech Mahindra: 15% EBIT margin by end-FY27, then a new phase announced.

Mahindra Finance: ₹3 lakh crore book by 2031 with a 70:30 mobility:non-wheels mix; ROA band 2.2–2.5% (at 2.4% now); ROE first milestone 15%. Used-vehicle disbursement share to climb back to 16–19% of incremental disbursements.
Mahindra Lifespaces: ₹10,000 cr pre-sales by FY30 (14x FY20); top-3/top-5 relative market share in Mumbai, Pune, Bangalore only.
Mahindra Logistics: remaining 2 lakh sq ft of white space to be sold by September; RIVIGO express EBITDA-positive "just around the corner" — CEO explicitly declined to name a month.
Aerostructures: Global Investor Day aspiration of 30x growth in a decade (10x organic) — "I can assure you we will grow faster than that."
order book & pipeline: Not an order-book business at the parent, but three hard pipeline metrics were given:

Aerostructures — $1.2 bn cumulative contract wins, of which $600 mn in the last year alone. Two large Airbus deals recently; single-source globally for the fuselage of two helicopters. Vinod Sahay's framing is the useful one: the industry takes 2–3 years to industrialise an award, so the book runs far ahead of revenue — "from an order-book standpoint we are actually a much bigger player than our revenue right now," against a global #1 sitting at ~4–4.5 (bn).

Real Estate GDV — ₹50,000 cr pipeline, up from ₹8,000 cr three years ago; ₹5,600 cr added this quarter alone (+60%), pre-sales ₹925 cr (2x). Anish Shah's point is that this fuel is already acquired — "the future growth is going to be driven by what we already have in place." Includes multi-use projects of ₹5,000 cr up to ₹10,000–12,000 cr each.

Auto demand vs supply — management refused to disclose enquiry/booking growth by powertrain or GST bracket ("it kind of gives an indication of… where demand momentum is"), conceding only "very strong demand momentum, urban and rural both." Dealer physical inventory ~15 days — thin, confirming the constraint is production not offtake. Tractor channel inventory 30–40 days, in line with norms (Swaraj below norm on supply issues).
segment / subsidiary detail: Auto — the new 3-column disclosure. For the first time management split auto into (1) core = ICE SUV + LCV, domestic + exports, at 8.9% PBIT; (2) EV = Mahindra Electric + M&M conversion income, at 5.3% / ₹288 cr PBIT; (3) others = trucks & buses, contract manufacturing for Last Mile Mobility, domestic + international subs. This is a material transparency upgrade — the ICE core margin was previously buried inside a blended number.
SUV — volumes +14.9% on an exceptional 22.1% Q1 FY26 base, despite production losses in April and May. Revenue market share held at the 24–25% line (LY Q1 was an outlier high).
LCV — volumes +20%, market share growing sequentially; #2 in <12t LCV bus (up from #3).

Trucks & Buses — volume +11%, market share 7.8%, but flagged as seasonally flattered: "market share is much higher for us in quarter one… because SML has a very strong bus queue, and the bus market is rallying in quarter one."
Last Mile Mobility (L5/3W) — volume 42,000, #1 position held, and the standout stat: L5 EV penetration at 40% vs ~27% a year ago, driven by the UDO.

EV / Born-Electric. Penetration 12% vs industry 9%; volumes +77%; XEV 9S is the single largest-selling EV across all passenger vehicles by volume despite its premium price point — management repeated this twice, and it is the strongest evidence they have that BEV demand is no longer price-floor-driven. Cumulative 77,000 EVs sold. The INGLO platform is the profitability lever: developed for a small number of vehicles but usable "across multiple top hats," so incremental model capex is low. Anish Shah's scale argument: ICE is running 9x EV volumes, and even at 1x the EV business is profitable ex-PLI.

Farm Equipment. Volume +18%, exports +15%, core tractor margin 19.2% inside the 17–19% band management says has held through both up- and down-cycles ("we have rarely gone below 17%, except maybe one quarter"). Farm machinery had its highest-ever quarter at ₹370 cr revenue — the mechanisation thesis showing up in the P&L. Horsepower mix has shifted hard: ~69–70% now in the 40–50 HP band, pulled by seeders and balers and helped by post-GST affordability ("they are able to buy a product with a higher horsepower for a price that they would have paid for a lower horsepower earlier"). International subsidiaries are the sore spot — a loss including the Erkunt Foundry impairment, now "solved for and exited," with remaining "weak spots" internationally acknowledged as a fix-list.

Rural demand construct (management's own six-point enabler chart): accelerating farm-labour shortage pushing mechanisation; wheat procurement +19% strengthening Rabi cash flows; rainfall deficit narrowed to 15% from much worse in June; reservoirs 7% below LPA but recovering; Kharif sowing shortfall only ~4%; government spending +16% plus state spends. Conclusion: "the data indicates a lot of negativity if you just look at the rainfall deficit, but because rains have actually come in, the sentiment is not negative."
Services & Growth Gems.

Mahindra Finance — PAT +78%; NIM rebuilt 6.5% → 7.3%; ROA 2.4%; GS2+GS3 below 10% for 7 consecutive quarters, GS2 (30+) down 100bps YoY. Book ~₹1.5 lakh cr, 83% wheels / 17% non-wheels; non-wheels +79%, housing finance +130% with housing GS3 now below 2.5%. Wheels growing ~20%. Used vehicles = 16% of incremental disbursements last quarter (band 15–19%), deliberately throttled while residual values reset post-GST; #1 in used tractor, #2–3 in used car.
Tech Mahindra — PAT +28%, EBIT margin 14.4%, FCF +94%, large-deal-led; geographic diversification and margin-gap closure the stated levers.

Mahindra Lifespaces — GDV +₹5,600 cr this quarter, pipeline ₹50,000 cr, pre-sales ₹925 cr (2x), OCs delivered ahead of schedule — 3,000 apartments OC'd, 1,500 delivered, 99% "zero-snag". Strategy is deliberately narrow: three cities (Mumbai/Pune/Bangalore = 55% of national unit volume), mid-premium and premium only, affordable exited. Measured on relative market share vs the biggest player, not absolute share. Slum redevelopment explicitly not prioritised today.

Mahindra Logistics — ₹14 cr profit at the M&M level, ₹25 cr at the business level — highest ever quarterly profit, after 11 straight quarters of losses through Q2 last year. The single biggest lever was white space cut from 16 lakh sq ft to 2 lakh sq ft, all sold not surrendered. RIVIGO express losses cut sharply, still a drag. Three very large e-com sites started this month. LOGIFREIGHT platform launched with ~5 customers signalling implementation.

Mahindra Aerostructures — see §4. Moving up the value chain from detailed parts → sub-assemblies → full fuselages, i.e. "from a manufacturer who used to make thousands of small parts, to making hundreds of high-value parts." Rated top-5 globally on quality/business excellence. An overseas acquisition is explicitly on the table, to be underwritten on returns.

SML Mahindra (truck & bus combination, announced 29-Jul-2026) — described as accretive, doubling the business's size, with network, product, cost and value-engineering synergies "already started working."
Mahindra Accelo — named as one of the three Growth Gems driving the +39% revenue / 3x profit, but not detailed on this call.

Named disruptions this quarter — 3 days of production lost in July to Maharashtra flooding (at least 2 days across all plants), a plant shutdown already scheduled in July, and a fire at a very large supplier in the South cutting off a critical part. "It didn't allow us to build inventory as well." The 8k EV capacity is also mix-exposed: "there's one product out of the three which is doing disproportionately well," so nameplate readiness ≠ shippable mix.
capital allocation: ROE is the discipline. 18% group target, 23% delivered, target deliberately not raised. Businesses are held to "profit standards… we need to be able to maintain ROA," with explicit long-duration leeway granted where the asset justifies it — aerospace was given a 10–15 year runway to profitability.

Exits are real, not rhetorical. Erkunt Foundry impaired and exited; Mahindra CIE stake sold (the gain sits in investments this quarter); Lifespaces exited the affordable segment. Anish Shah recounted the truck & bus history as the template: "Let's decide whether we want this business or not… if they cannot, we will exit" — the business executed, so it got SML instead of the axe.
Inorganic is live in exactly one place: a global acquisition in Aerostructures, to be underwritten on returns, driven by what OEM customers want Mahindra to become.
SML Mahindra combination described as accretive with cost/value-engineering synergies.
No dividend, buyback, leverage or consolidated-capex-rupee number was given on this call.
risks & watch-items: Commodity volatility, unhedgeable in Farm. Steel +24%, rubber +30% (+53% CYTD). Management's own hedge against being wrong: "if you believe the war is going to continue for the next 6 months, then we may have bigger problems, the whole economy… will have bigger problems."

Supply-chain fragility is the binding constraint on the capacity ladder. Stated capacity includes supplier capacity, "and that's not always happening." Fire at a South supplier, floods, and shutdowns all hit inside one month.
Farm Q2 is pre-warned down on the festive shift + commodities — the one place management refused to guide optimistically.

PLI taper is management's own base case. They are voluntarily telling the government the subsidy should shrink as EV margins scale. EV margin at 5.3% is not yet ICE-level, so the taper timing (clarity in 6–12 months) is a genuine earnings variable.
Monsoon still unresolved. 15% rainfall deficit, reservoirs 7% below LPA, Kharif sowing ~4% behind. "We need to see what happens to rainfall and other factors over the next two months."
Farm market share slipped off the 45.2% all-time high — acknowledged, not explained.
International farm subsidiaries remain loss-making beyond Erkunt; "we still have a certain set of weak spots."
RIVIGO express is still a drag with no dated turnaround — CEO deliberately withheld a month.
EV mix concentration — one of three EV products is doing "disproportionately well," so capacity readiness may not convert.
Disclosure withheld: absolute PLI contribution, enquiry/booking growth by powertrain or GST bracket, and consolidated absolute revenue/PAT on the call.
management quality / tone: The tell of this call is the format change: Anish Shah put seven business CEOs on stage — Sahay, Sikka, Nakra, Sinha, Velusamy, Rebello — and said it will be the format going forward, so investors "yourself be able to assess the quality of talent that we have." A holdco discount is fundamentally a bet against management depth; putting the bench on stage is a direct, structural answer to it.

Tone was "cautiously optimistic" — the exact phrase used to open and close. Specific credibility markers: refusing to reset the 18% ROE target upward after a 23% print; volunteering the ex-CIE 22% number rather than letting 34% stand; disclosing the auto 3-column margin split for the first time, which exposes the 8.9% core rather than hiding it; conceding the hedging-adjusted ~8% underlying margin when an analyst constructed it; and pushing back numerically rather than vaguely when Binay built a 650–700bps headwind ("I wouldn't get to 600-700. I think 400-500"). Jejurikar volunteered the July production losses with visible reluctance ("I was avoiding wanting to say this") — unforced disclosure of bad news.

Where they closed up: Jejurikar bluntly refused the enquiry/booking cut — "You really want to know everything about our business… it kind of gives an indication of… where demand momentum is." Sikka refused to date the RIVIGO breakeven. Shah refused a PLI timeline. Each refusal was stated as a refusal, not disguised as an answer.
non-obvious takeaways: The 34% PAT headline is 22% after the CIE gain — and management said so unprompted. Anyone anchoring on 34% is anchoring on an asset sale. The genuinely impressive number is that 22% was delivered while eating 450bps of auto commodity inflation.

The hedging loss is bullish, and the market will likely read it backwards. An 85bps MTM loss on aluminium hedges exists only because spot aluminium fell ~20% in 8–10 days. The loss is the receipt for the input relief that shows up in Q2 COGS. Reported margin 7.1%, underlying ~8%, and the delta reverses.

First-time 3-column disclosure is a governance signal disguised as a slide. Splitting core ICE (8.9%) from EV (5.3%) from others removes management's own ability to hide EV dilution inside a blended number. Companies volunteer that structure when they expect the split to improve — i.e. it's a forward-confidence tell about EV margin convergence.

The Lifespaces "15% price premium on trust" is the group's most under-priced asset. A real-estate developer monetising an automotive brand's trust is textbook conglomerate synergy that almost never actually shows up in numbers. The ₹12,000 cr JDA won on brand alone is the same asset in a second form.

Owned GPUs change the AI unit economics. "We don't need to pay for tokens" means AI deployment scales at fixed cost, not variable cost — the opposite of peers renting frontier-model inference. Combined with 19 proprietary models trained on 20 years of proprietary simulation data, this is a cost and differentiation position, and it is invisible in the P&L today.

L5 EV penetration at 40% (from 27%) is running ~3x the PV rate and gets a single line on the call. Last Mile Mobility is quietly the group's most electrified business and its economics are TCO-driven — a far more durable adoption base than PV.

Mahindra Finance's Q1 PAT contribution exceeded Farm's (213 vs Farm's, per the contribution chart Shah pointed at). The market still prices M&M as an SUV-and-tractor company; the earnings mix has already moved.
Season shift to 11-Oct means Q2 tractor volume is arithmetically pre-committed to disappoint and Q3 to flatter. Any read on FY27 farm demand off the Q2 print alone will be wrong in both directions.

The capacity plan is a demand statement in disguise. Committing to 2x by FY31 with Nagpur greenfield only makes sense if management believes today's 15-day dealer inventory is structural, not cyclical.
qoq change log (fill each quarter): Q1 FY27 (this): First transcript-based note on M&M — the prior companies.csv entry was a profile-only row (latestquarter = profile, last updated 2026-06-27) describing Auto + Farm + EV + Construction Equipment with themes of electric mobility, rural demand, AI-driven operations and SUV leadership. This call confirms and quantifies all four of those profile themes for the first time: EV penetration 12% vs industry 9% with EV PBIT ₹288 cr; rural enabler chart (wheat procurement +19%, govt spend +16%, deficit narrowed to 15%); AI with disclosed outcome metrics on owned GPUs; SUV volume +14.9% with revenue market share at 24–25%. It also materially extends the profile: the sub-segment list must now carry Growth Gems (Real Estate, Logistics, Aerostructures, Accelo) and Last Mile Mobility, and the entity list must add SML Mahindra (combination announced 29-Jul-2026) while dropping Mahindra CIE (stake sold) and Erkunt Foundry (impaired and exited). Headline: consolidated PAT +34% (+22% ex-CIE gain), revenue +28%, ROE 23% vs 18% target, EPS ₹48. Auto core PBIT margin compressed to 8.9% (from 10.2%/10.8%) on 450bps commodity inflation plus an 85bps hedging MTM loss; Farm consolidated 14.2% with core tractor at 19.2%. Every subsidiary engine positive: MMFS +78%, TechM +28%, Growth Gems 3x. Capacity ladder set out for the first time in dated form: 64.5k → 68k by Sep-26 → 82k by end-FY27 → 92k → 2x by FY31 with Nagpur phase 1 in H1 CY2029.

Q2 FY27 → check: (1) did Auto OPM "maintain/slightly improve" sequentially off the 7.1% reported / ~8% hedge-adjusted base, as promised — and did the 85bps hedging loss actually reverse into a buffer; (2) did Farm deliver only the pre-warned "temporary blip," or worse, given the 11-Oct festive shift moved peak tractor volume into Q3; (3) was 68,000 units/month capacity operationally ready by September (60k ICE + 8k EV) — this is the first hard, dated commitment to test; (4) did the 2.7% July auto price hike stick without demand damage (dealer inventory was only ~15 days); (5) Mahindra Logistics — were the last 2 lakh sq ft of white space sold by September, and did RIVIGO express turn EBITDA positive ("just around the corner"); (6) Farm market share vs the 45.2% all-time high, and whether international subs stopped bleeding post-Erkunt exit; (7) any PLI-taper clarity inside the stated 6–12 month window; (8) monsoon resolution against the 15% deficit / 4% Kharif sowing shortfall; (9) did EV penetration hold above 12% and did the XEV 9S keep the #1 PV-EV slot; (10) NUIQ segment finally named ahead of the FY28 launch.

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
themes.driver: Capacity commissioning against demand (TVSMOTOR 2W to 8.3mn by Q4FY27, BAJAJ-AUTO 7m to 9m+ units); 3W/2W EV penetration inflection; GST-2.0 price-cut demand, aged-fleet replacement and festive 2W/PV.

hero.oneLiner: The deck positions M&M as a multi-engine group — market-leading Auto (SUV/LCV) and Farm franchises plus Finance, Tech and "Growth Gems" (Real Estate, Accelo, Logistics, Trucks & Buses, Aerostructures) — delivering "Acceleration in Uncertainty" through commodity inflation via scale, leadership share and an AI-led transformation.
